summary: This note is an overview of the Los Angeles Dodgers, an American professional baseball team in Major League Baseball's National League West. It covers the franchise's championship and award record, its founding in Brooklyn in 1883, and its move to Los Angeles before the 1958 season. It also lists the Brooklyn and Los Angeles pennant and World Series years.
one_line: Overview of the Los Angeles Dodgers, a Major League Baseball team in the National League West, covering its titles, award winners, and move from Brooklyn to Los Angeles.
key_facts: The Dodgers have won six World Series titles and 22 National League pennants as a franchise.
11 NL MVP award winners have played for the Dodgers, winning a total of 13 MVP Awards.
Eight Cy Young Award winners have pitched for the Dodgers, winning a total of twelve Cy Young Awards.
The Dodgers have produced 18 Rookie of the Year Award winners, twice as many as the next closest team.
The Dodgers had four consecutive Rookie of the Year Award winners from 1979 to 1982 and five consecutive from 1992 to 1996.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are an American professional baseball team based in Los Angeles, California.
The Dodgers compete in Major League Baseball as a member club of the National League West division.
The team was established in 1883 in Brooklyn, New York, and moved to Los Angeles before the 1958 season.
The Dodgers played four seasons at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum before moving to Dodger Stadium in 1962.
In Brooklyn, the Dodgers won the NL pennant in 1890, 1899, 1900, 1916, 1920, 1941, 1947, 1949, 1952, 1953, 1955 and 1956.
The Dodgers won the World Series in 1955 while based in Brooklyn.
After moving to Los Angeles, the Dodgers won World Series championships in 1959, 1963, 1965, 1981 and 1988.
The Dodgers won National League pennants in Los Angeles in 1959, 1963, 1965, 1966, 1974, 1977, 1978, 1981, 1988 and 2017.
In all, the Dodgers have appeared in 19 World Series: nine in Brooklyn and ten in Los Angeles.
